newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 2.

text.p: The following are the top stories in the Irish press on Thursday.
- The government will take legal action to close BUPA's operations in the Irish Republic if talks fail to resolve a dispute over the legality of some of BUPA's products.

- The Irish national debt has fallen for the first time in 39 years and the debt-to-GDP ratio has tumbled more than eight percent, propelling Ireland towards qualification for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), the National Treasury Management Agency (NTMA) said.
- Exchequer figures to be published tomorrow will show the healthiest position in more than 20 years, with a strong surplus on the current budget.
- The Exchequer tax take soared last year by well over one billion punts, according to figures to be released tomorrow by the Department of Finance.

- Any hope of an early breakthrough in the Northern Ireland peace process has virtually disappeared, British and Irish sources conceded last night after an Irish Republican Army landmine was found in the grounds of Belfast castle.
- There has been a sharp drop in confidence among small and medium-sized companies, according to the Irish Small and Medium Enterprises Association (ISME).
